patients.summary: Construction laborer with advanced HIV who has declined antiretroviral therapy since a brief course in 2016, asplenic after a 2011 crash, on TMP-SMX prophylaxis he takes unevenly. Develops HIV-associated mixed cryoglobulinemia with neuropathy and renal involvement in 2023, then pulmonary and cutaneous nocardiosis in May 2026 and CNS nocardiosis with an ICU stay in July 2026, when ART is finally started.

documents.title: Records from Prior Clinic
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Faxed records, 38 pages, from the community health clinic he used before. Summary for the PCP:
- HIV-1 infection diagnosed 2016 at that clinic. Started on an antiretroviral regimen at diagnosis, notes say he stopped it on his own within the first year; repeated counseling documented, he declined restarting.
- CD4 below 200 on their last several draws; viral load in the tens of thousands.
- On TMP-SMX DS three times weekly for PCP prophylaxis.
- Anemia attributed to chronic disease; mild CKD on their problem list.
- MVC around 2011: both femurs fixed, spleen removed, several transfusions. Right knee arthritis since.
- Hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccine series documented as complete.
- NKDA.
Records placed in chart for review at the 9/20 visit.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

45 y/o man here to set up primary care. Old clinic records reviewed (arrived 9/14).

HIV: diagnosed 2016. Took ART for a few months back then, didn't like how it made him feel and stopped; hasn't been on anything since. Knows his counts are low. Takes Bactrim DS M/W/F "most weeks" - honest that he forgets some. No current fevers, sweats, cough, thrush, diarrhea or skin problems.
Other: anemia (told it's from the HIV), mild kidney disease on old list, right knee arthritis after the 2011 crash - uses ibuprofen 400 or Tylenol 500 when the knee acts up on the job.

PSH: 2011 MVC - ORIF both femurs, splenectomy, multiple transfusions. 
Meds: TMP-SMX DS 1 tab three times weekly; ibuprofen 400 q6h prn; acetaminophen 500 q6h prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father - HTN, CAD. Mother - type 2 DM, hypothyroid. No immunodeficiency, autoimmune or bleeding disorders in the family.
SH: laborer for a construction outfit, lives alone in Amherst. Quit cigarettes about 8 yrs ago. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a month. 

Exam: well-appearing, thin. No oral thrush or lesions. No lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear. RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, healed midline scar, no organomegaly. Old scars both thighs. R knee with crepitus, no effusion, full extension. Skin without rash. Feet: normal sensation.

A/P
1. HIV, advanced, off ART. Long talk. Explained that modern once-daily regimens are much easier than what he took in 2016 and that being off treatment with low CD4 is the biggest risk to his health. He's not ready - wants to "think about it." Offered HIV clinic referral, declined for now. Will check CD4/VL today and keep raising it.
2. PCP prophylaxis - continue TMP-SMX DS three times weekly; set phone alarm.
3. Asplenia + HIV - needs pneumococcal, meningococcal ACWY and B, Hib. Nurse visit in Oct with flu shot.
4. Anemia of chronic disease - CBC.
5. CKD 2 - CMP, UA, urine albumin.
6. R knee post-traumatic arthritis - ibuprofen/APAP prn as before.
7. Hep C screen today. Hep A/B vaccination documented in old records.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Todd - your labs are back. Your CD4 count is low and the virus is very active in your blood, which is what we expected off treatment. Your blood count shows the same mild anemia as before, kidney function is about where your old records had it, and hepatitis C screen is negative. Cholesterol is fine. My offer stands on getting you back on HIV medicine whenever you're ready - one pill a day these days. Please keep taking the Bactrim. See you in October for shots.

orders.reason: suspected cryoglobulinemic vasculitis with renal involvement

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, achy joints, dark urine, rash on legs.

HPI: 47M with advanced HIV (off ART) and CKD 2. Over roughly three months he has been getting more and more worn out. Urine has been the color of strong tea most days. Lately both hands, wrists and knees swell a little and hurt enough that he's had to cut back hours. Red spots on his lower legs come and go - worse when he's been working outside in the cold - and they don't fade when he presses on them. For the last few weeks his feet tingle and feel weak; he can't walk a long distance like before. No fever at home that he knows of, no cough, no new meds. Still on Bactrim (most doses), ibuprofen for the joints more often than usual.

Exam: T 37.8, BP 115/70, HR 90. Tired-appearing. Mouth clear. Lungs clear. RRR. Abdomen benign. Joints: mild symmetric puffiness of wrists and MCPs, both knees, no hot joint. Skin: numerous palpable purpuric papules both shins below the knees, non-blanching. Neuro: vibration reduced at both great toes and ankles; strength grossly intact, reflexes present.

A/P:
1. Palpable purpura + arthralgias + hematuria/proteinuria + neuropathy in untreated HIV: picture fits cryoglobulinemic vasculitis. Hep B and C need excluding (he had multiple transfusions in 2011). Sending CMP, UA with micro, CBC, C4, serum cryoglobulins (kept warm, lab aware), HBsAg, HCV Ab, urine albumin, CD4/VL.
2. Peripheral neuropathy, new - likely part of the same process.
3. Kidneys - expect creatinine up; will refer to rheumatology now and review once labs back.
4. HIV - this may well be driven by uncontrolled virus. ART is the real treatment; raised it again. He'll "look at it" once we know more.
Will call with results this week.

documents.title: Results Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt with results. Cryoglobulins positive. C4 low at 5. Creatinine 1.35 (up from his ~1.1 baseline). UA 2+ protein, 2+ blood, 15 RBC/hpf. Hep B surface Ag and Hep C Ab both negative. Hgb at his usual mild-anemia level.
Dx: cryoglobulinemia with skin, joint, nerve and kidney involvement, most likely from untreated HIV since hepatitis is ruled out. Rheumatology referral already sent - urged him to keep it. Told him again that HIV treatment is the main fix. He asked good questions, still undecided. Repeat BMP/UA in a couple of months.

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 01/10/2024
Referred by: primary care, for positive cryoglobulins

Thank you for sending Mr. McKenna, a 47-year-old construction laborer with HIV diagnosed in 2016, off antiretrovirals for years.

History: since late summer, fatigue, dark urine, symmetric small- and large-joint arthralgia with mild swelling, an intermittent cold-provoked purpuric eruption of the shins, and distal paresthesias with some foot weakness. Splenectomy and transfusions after a 2011 crash.
Medications: TMP-SMX DS three times weekly, ibuprofen 400 mg as needed, acetaminophen 500 mg as needed. Allergies: none known.

Exam: afebrile. Faint residual palpable purpura on both shins. Mild synovial thickening at the wrists without effusion. Knees cool. Decreased vibration at the toes.

Data reviewed from your office (11/13/23): serum cryoglobulins positive, C4 5 mg/dL, creatinine 1.35, urinalysis 2+ protein and 2+ blood with 15 RBC/hpf, HBsAg and HCV antibody negative.

Impression: mixed cryoglobulinemia with cutaneous vasculitis, arthralgia, peripheral neuropathy and renal involvement. With hepatitis B and C excluded, untreated HIV is the most likely driver.

Recommendations:
1. The treatment of the underlying cause is antiretroviral therapy; I recommended an HIV clinic. He declined that referral today.
2. Given a CD4 well under 200, I would not add glucocorticoids or other immunosuppression.
3. Keep following renal function and urinalysis with you.
I am glad to see him again as needed.

Allergies: NKDA.

- Rheumatology

documents.title: Outside Consult Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rheum letter reviewed. Agree - ART is the answer, no immunosuppression. Will see him next month.

S: Saw rheumatology in Jan. Rash has quieted over the winter, joints a little better, still tired. Feet still tingle. Urine "lighter some days." He did not want the HIV clinic referral the rheumatologist offered. Bactrim: misses doses most weeks, by his own count.
O: Afebrile. No purpura today. Mild wrist puffiness. Lungs clear. Reduced vibration at toes, unchanged.
A/P:
- Cryoglobulinemia, HIV-associated: no immunosuppression per rheum. Only real treatment is ART. Declined again today.
- Medication noncompliance: added to problem list - declining ART since 2016 and irregular with prophylaxis. Non-judgmental talk about barriers (work hours, bad memories of old regimen). Pill box, alarms.
- Kidneys: BMP, UA today.
- Neuropathy: watch, foot care.
RTC 3-4 months.

OUTSIDE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Date of visit: 05/06/2026

CC: cough and fever x3 weeks; painful lump right forearm.
HPI: 50M with advanced HIV not on antiretroviral therapy, asplenic, on TMP-SMX prophylaxis (reports missed doses). Three weeks of productive cough, fevers and weight loss. About a week ago noticed what he thought was a pimple on the right forearm; it has since grown into a tender swollen lump.
PMH: HIV/AIDS, cryoglobulinemia, CKD 2, anemia of chronic disease, peripheral neuropathy. PSH: bilateral femur ORIF and splenectomy after 2011 MVC.
Meds: TMP-SMX DS three times weekly, ibuprofen prn, acetaminophen prn. Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals on arrival: T 38.2 C (100.8 F), BP 125/80, RR 22.
Exam: ill-appearing, speaking full sentences. Scattered crackles right base. Right forearm: single fluctuant, erythematous, tender nodule. No other skin lesions. Neuro nonfocal, alert and oriented.
Results: WBC 9.0, Hgb 12.5, CD4 120. Sputum Gram stain: filamentous gram-positive rods, weakly acid-fast. CXR: patchy RLL infiltrates.

ED course / impression: pulmonary nocardiosis with a cutaneous (forearm) lesion in advanced HIV. Infectious disease consulted by phone. Admitted to medicine.

- Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HOSPITAL DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/06/2026 via the emergency department. Discharged 05/09/2026.

Diagnoses: pulmonary nocardiosis; cutaneous nocardiosis, right forearm (HIV-related opportunistic skin infection); advanced HIV, not on ART.

Course: admitted with three weeks of cough, fever and weight loss and a fluctuant right forearm nodule; sputum smear showed filamentous gram-positive, weakly acid-fast rods and the culture grew Nocardia species. Defervesced within 48 hours on treatment-dose trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Forearm lesion smaller and less tender at discharge. Breathing comfortably on room air.

Discharge medications:
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS (800/160 mg), 2 tablets by mouth twice daily, planned for at least 6 months (replaces the three-times-weekly prophylaxis dose)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed
- Ibuprofen 400 mg every 6 hours as needed (home medication, continued)
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Follow-up: infectious disease clinic appointment arranged; antiretroviral therapy to be started there. Primary care follow-up advised.

- Hospital Medicine

Offered a visit with PCP; he'd rather wait until he's back to work. Told to call for fever, headache, confusion or worse breathing.

OUTSIDE HOSPITAL DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 07/13/2026 (ICU, then medical floor). Discharged 08/11/2026.

Principal diagnosis: nocardiosis, pulmonary with central nervous system involvement (right frontal brain abscess).
Other: advanced HIV/AIDS, antiretroviral therapy started this admission; HIV-associated cryoglobulinemia; CKD stage 2; anemia of chronic disease; peripheral neuropathy; asplenia.

Presentation: 50-year-old man treated for pulmonary and cutaneous nocardiosis two months ago, who stopped his oral antibiotic after a few weeks. Two weeks of cough, fever and increasing breathlessness, with a severe headache and spells of confusion. On arrival T 38.9 C, BP 110/70, HR 102, RR 22. Crackles at the right base; mildly disoriented to time and place, no focal weakness. WBC 12.0, Hgb 13.2, platelets 250, CD4 50 cells/mm3, HIV viral load 120,000 copies/mL. CXR right lower lobe infiltrate. Sputum Gram stain with branching filamentous organisms; culture grew Nocardia species. MRI brain: single 1.6 cm ring-enhancing right frontal lesion, mild edema, no shift.

Course: ICU for close neurologic monitoring. IV trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole plus IV imipenem. Headache and confusion resolved over the first week; transferred to the floor. Infectious disease started bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 50/200/25 mg daily on 07/28. Tolerating all medications at discharge, oriented, ambulating, on room air.

Discharge medications:
- Bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 50/200/25 mg, 1 tablet daily
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS (800/160 mg), 2 tablets by mouth three times daily, for at least 12 months
- Acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Follow-up: infectious disease clinic in 2 weeks, with repeat brain MRI and labs arranged by ID. Primary care within 4 weeks.

- Critical Care / Hospital Medicine
